title: Public Wi-Fi Snooping
summary: Free Wi-Fi networks in airports and coffee shops are rarely encrypted. Anyone nearby can use simple tools to read your unencrypted traffic. Always use a VPN or stick to mobile data when banking.

title: Spotting Fake Login Links
summary: Scammers disguise links using lookalike letters, like replacing an English 'o' with a Cyrillic character. Always check the exact address bar carefully before typing your email and password.

title: Beware of Sticky QR Codes
summary: Criminals paste malicious QR code stickers over authentic parking meter or restaurant codes. Always look closely for peeling edges and preview the link before opening it in your browser.

title: Revoke Needless Permissions
summary: Games and torch utilities rarely need access to your contact list, microphone, or SMS messages. Check your phone settings monthly to turn off permissions apps do not actually need.

title: Juice Jacking at Charging Ports
summary: Public USB charging stations can transfer data along with electricity. Criminals modify public ports to install malware. Use your own wall charger adapter or a USB data blocker.
